question: to the Commission Dimitris Tsiodras (PPE) Subject:

In 2025, Europe experienced the worst wildfire season on record1. Specifically, 1 079 538 hectares – equivalent to approximately the area of Cyprus – were ravaged by fire across several EU Member States. Meanwhile, the size and intensity of the fires are increasing and the likelihood of very large fires or ‘megafires’ is expected to more than double by the end of the century. This situation calls for a drastic increase in European instruments and further use of innovative technologies to prevent, detect and respond to fires and strengthen the EU’s resilience. In light of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.
What is its forecast for an increase in resources and instruments to improve fire prevention and response?
How will it support EU Member States in planning prevention and preparedness measures, including tools and systems for early warnings and forest management?
How does it intend to use programmes such as Horizon Europe to support research and the adoption of innovative technologies in the field of integrated fire risk management?
Joint Research Centre of the European Commission.
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (14.7.2026) Under cohesion funds, in the current Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF), EUR 3.1 billion are available for prevention and preparedness, notably for forest fires. The proposal for a new Union Civil Protection Mechanism and Health Emergency Response instrument under the new MFF includes a budget of EUR 10.7 billion to enhance the EU’s capacity to respond to disasters, including wildfires. The European Forest Fire Information System1 addresses wildfire risk. The Union Civil Protection Mechanism2 coordinates the deployment of assistance. Activities under the EU Mission on Adaptation to Climate Change3 provide good examples of testing and deployment of solutions. Horizon Europe4 supported a cluster of five projects on integrated wildfire risk management with researchers, practitioners and public bodies. In the next MFF, resilience to climate change, prevention, detection and response to wildfires may remain a priority in the programme. Measures to foster an integrated approach to wildfire risk management were published in March 20265. In cohesion policy, under Regional Emergency Support to Reconstruction (RESTORE)6, 22 programmes7 mobilised more than EUR 1.8 billion for investments and other actions for reconstruction in response to natural disasters. Out of this, EUR 93 million were allocated for adaptation to climate change, prevention and management of climate risks in case of fires. The EU Solidarity Fund (EUSF)8 provided EUR 2.3 million to Cyprus after the wildfires in 20259. Through the Horizon Europe Work Programme on Cluster 3 ‘Civil Security for Society’, the development of innovative solutions and operational capabilities are supported to strengthen Europe’s resilience. The EUSF may cover a part of the costs for emergency and recovery operations incurred by public authorities.
